scope: Theorem 3.1 (Compact support and rapid decay) of the manuscript “Computation under Rapidly Vanishing Navier–Stokes Forcing” (preprints/Computation-under-Rapidly-Vanishing-Navier-Stokes-Forcing-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 931c07840228968b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity ν. From a deterministic Turing machine M and a finite input w one can effectively construct a smooth force on [0, ∞) × R3, supported for all times in the fixed compact set K = [−2, 1] × [−1, 2] × [−1, 1], such that, for every pair of nonnegative integers J, l and spatial multi-index α, sup t≥0, x∈R3 (1 + t)J ∂l t∂α x f(t, x) < ∞. (5) The Navier–Stokes equation with this force and zero initial velocity has an explicit global smooth solution, unique in the finite-interval class (2). Its material trajectory from the origin satisfies M halts on w ⇐⇒ X1(t, 0) < −1 for some t ≥ 0. (6) The velocity has the same fixed support and rapid mixed-derivative bounds. The pressure is zero. The force is a general body force. Because K is fixed, the same bounds hold with (1 + t + |x|)J in place of (1 + t)J .
